mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2.5% annualized over the past 3 months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% over the past 3 months signals a tightening labor market, which historically leads to wage inflation and increased corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE decrease > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 6 months signals robust economic demand, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with subsequent economic activity indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a restrictive monetary policy environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS > 4% and rising CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent restrictive monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the interaction of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent labor market strength.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% over the past 3 months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease > 1% does not correlate with subsequent consumer demand indicators.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 2% over the past 6 months and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it signals a supply-side contraction coupled with restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decrease > 2% in 6 months and FEDFUNDS > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of INDPRO decrease and FEDFUNDS > 3% does not correlate with subsequent economic contraction.
